display.title: Episode 198: Nachum Ish Gamzu and the Strange Gift
display.summary_short: How a mezuzah is made, a phone quiz, Shema with a first-grade class, and a bedtime story of Nachum Ish Gamzu's box of sand: 'this too is for the good'.
display.summary_long: The show opens straight into the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message. Mitzvah Time teaches how a mezuzah is made: it must be written on parchment from the skin of a kosher animal, never on paper, with a quill from a kosher bird and specially prepared black ink. A listener from a Boro Park girls' school then answers a phone quiz on last week's lesson about Shin-Dalet-Yud. A first-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park leads the Shema. Story time is a bedtime scene: little Yehoshua tells his father how Hashem turned Avraham Avinu's dust and straw into arrows and swords, and his father answers with a similar story. Nachum Ish Gamzu, who always said 'gam zu l'tovah', this too is for the good, sets out to ask a king to let the Jews keep the Torah, carrying a golden box of diamonds. At an inn the diamonds are stolen and replaced with sand. The furious king condemns him, but Eliyahu HaNavi, disguised as an officer, suggests trying the 'miracle sand' in battle, and the war is won. The thieving innkeeper brings wagonloads of sand and is punished when it proves to be ordinary. The show ends with the 'My Mezuzah' contest reminder.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem does is for the good: gam zu l'tovah.

date.note: Three weeks after 195 (Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan, 1985-10-15); the quiz reviews 196's lesson; contest runs until Chanukah. Matches the count back from 211.

advisories.note: A king forbids Torah study; Nachum Ish Gamzu is jailed and sentenced to death before being saved.
The thieving innkeeper is put to death by the king.

privacy.note: Phone-quiz winner gives her first name and school; a class teacher is named.
